data.text:
🇵🇭 Why We Still Love the Philippines

We love our country not because it is perfect, but because it is ours.

We love it despite the corruption that stains our institutions—because the soul of the nation is not found in its politics, but in its people. In the quiet dignity of farmers, the resilience of nurses abroad, the laughter of children playing in flooded streets. We love it because it is home.

We love it despite the daily bickering, the noise of division on social media—because beneath the clamor lies a shared longing: to be heard, to be healed, to belong. We are a family still learning how to speak truth with grace, and to listen with compassion.

We love this country even as it is battered by typhoons, earthquakes, and fire—because we have seen it rise again and again. Our land may break, but our spirit does not. Each storm leaves scars, but also seeds of resilience, teaching us to rebuild with deeper faith and stronger unity.

We love the Philippines because our heroes once did. Because they believed in a future worth dying for. Because we carry their blood, their dreams, their unfinished fight. Their courage reminds us that healing is not only possible—it is our duty.

Patriotism is not blind loyalty—it is stubborn hope. It is choosing to stay, to speak, to serve, even when it hurts. It is believing that we are still capable of greatness, and that the best chapters of our story are yet to be written.

We must not stop.
We must step up.
We must heal what is broken, and lift what has fallen.

Who knows—perhaps God and our true heroes are watching, waiting for us to rise. And when we do, it will not be because we ignored our wounds, but because we turned them into wisdom, courage, and love.

The Philippines is not just a place—it is a promise. And that promise is worth keeping.

Tony Leachon

data.text:
ROAD CLOSURES IN INTRAMUROS

Following a fire in Intramuros, Manila on February 25, the Intramuros Administration announced that some roads will be closed. It likewise recommended Beaterio, Anda, Sta. Potenciana, and Solana streets as alternate routes.

According to reports, the blaze reached the fourth alarm, while authorities have yet to determine the cause.
